title: Fingerprints: edits that make a finding new
description: The other half of the "What changes the fingerprint" table of BEP 1498: an identical line added, the flagged line edited, wrapped or joined, a space inside a string, and the file or the package renamed. Each edit starts from the base sources and is scanned against the baseline created first; [gate] failOnSeverity = "LOW" makes each scan with a new finding exit 1. The issues: ballerina:13 on the module-level password (line 1), on dbPassword and on the multi-line apiSecret template, and ballerina:1 on the checkpanic in main. A renamed rule ID also changes the fingerprint but cannot be shown with a fixture. Needs scan 0.15.0+.
upstream: BEP 1498: Finding fingerprints and baseline adoption (ballerina-spec/beps/tool-scan/1498_scan_baseline.md)

steps.name: Scan: identical line added above
steps.note: A second `_ = checkpanic getResult();` above the first. Both have the same hash; matching is by count, so the LAST one in source order (:2) is new, whichever was added. Expect 1 new issue(s), 4 in baseline, exit 1.

steps.name: Scan: flagged line edited
steps.note: "admin123" -> "admin1234". The edited code is reviewed again: 1 new issue(s), 3 in baseline, and a warning that 1 entry matches no issue.

steps.name: Scan: space added inside a string
steps.note: "hunter2" -> "hunter 2". String contents are hashed as written, so this is a different fingerprint (if the rule still flags the value; a value that no longer looks like a secret only leaves a stale entry).

steps.name: Scan: flagged line wrapped
steps.note: The literal moves to its own line, which is now the first flagged line, with different tokens: 1 new, 3 in baseline, 1 stale.

steps.name: Flagged line joined with the next
Scan: flagged line joined with the next
steps.note: `string dbPassword = "admin123"; return dbPassword;` on one line: different tokens, 1 new, 1 stale.

steps.name: Scan: file renamed
steps.note: The path is hashed, so all 4 findings are new and all 4 entries are stale.

steps.name: Scan: package renamed
steps.note: The organization and name are hashed, so all 4 findings are new. No stale warning: the old package's entries are outside the scope of the run (that package was not scanned), so they are unknown, not stale.
